description: 200-task diversity batch tuned with div1/div2 pass@16: the agent must look up every target (never named in the instruction) through a bounded lookup (~20 agent steps), 15% hard 3-skill chains, 10-20 action golden paths, fewer short official-like intents, open pairs weighted by div1+div2 pass@16 (saturated skill sets down-weighted). DeepSeek V4 Pro authors, Claude Opus verifies.
difficulty: derived from the skill chain (medium or hard)
difficulty_rule: Batch-5 rule: medium = 2 skills (at least one retrieval and one action); hard = 3+ skills with two distinct retrievals or one retrieval feeding two dependent actions, plus metadata.hard_criteria with >= 2 entries. A HARD slot must ship a hard task; never pad a chain.
extra_rules: This batch must be learnable or hard for the current policy: div1's always-solved tasks named their target ('Ship order 000000304') and needed 3-7 clicks on one page. Make the agent search, filter, count, compare or follow a link chain to find what to act on.

But keep it reachable: in div2, 54 of 200 tasks were never solved in 16 tries, mostly reddit lookups that meant scanning every comment or post (72% of those rollouts hit the 50-step cap). A good div3 task needs 10-20 deliberate actions, not an open-ended crawl.
